To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of Rantes, TNF- α, MDA and nitric oxide are increased in hepatitis C virus-infected patients, and that the increase in RANTES, TNFa, MDA and Nitric oxide is associated with hematological abnormalities.
RANTES and tumor necrosis factor α are associated with oxidative stress and hematological abnormalities in HCV infection.
RANTES, TNFA, MDA, NO, and hematological abnormalities are associated with hepatitis C virus infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of chemokine and oxidative stress as potential markers for monitoring HCV infection and the role of these markers in the hematological abnormalities that occur in these patients.
the relationship between HCV infection and hematological abnormalities and their correlation with RANTES, TNFa, MDA, NO, and HCV viral load.
the association between RANTES and the oxidative stress in chronic hepatitis C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCV infection is associated with a systemic oxidative stress and hematological abnormalities that might be used as a marker of disease severity.
the present findings support the concept that HCV-induced oxidative stress, RANTES, and TNF-α are involved in the pathogenesis of hematological abnormalities in HCV infection.

the increased levels of RANTE and tumor necrosis factor-alpha and oxidative stress (MDA and NO) are associated with the severity of the infection and the degree of liver damage, which is reflected in the hematological parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the levels of chemokine (RANTES, MDA and TNF-α) were significantly higher in HCV patients compared with the controls, and there was positive correlation between the levels of chemotactic factors (RANTES and TNF- α) and HCV RNA viral loads.

the levels of Rantes, TNF- α, MDA and No in HCV infected patients showed a significant positive correlation with HCV RNA viral loads, while the complete blood picture in these patients showed mild leukopenia, thrombocytosis and lymphocytopenia with consequent significant increases in the lymphocytes/ neutrophils ratio.
the HCV-induced oxidative stress and inflammation may play a major role in the development of hematological abnormalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RANTES, TN-α, MDA and No levels may serve as monitoring markers of the disease severity.

the levels of RANTEs, TNF- a, MDA and NOS were increased in HCV patients and that these levels showed positive correlation with HCV viral load, which may indicate a relationship between the increased level of these markers and the severity of the infection.
RANTES, TNFA, oxidative stress, and hematological abnormalities may be used as monitoring tools for the assessment of HCV infection.
